title: Georgia man sues Flock, sheriff's office over alleged ALPR-fueled retaliation
summary: Georgia small-business owner Tyler Murkerson has sued Flock and the Coweta County Sheriff's Office, alleging deputies conducted repeated warrantless ALPR searches of his vehicle in retaliation for an earlier excessive-force lawsuit, using nonsense justifications like 'info' and '37' in Flock's free-text field. The complaint highlights Flock's lack of case-number requirements, which the company announced in August 2026 it would fix by year-end, and notes three sheriff's office employees resigned during an internal audit.

key_quotes.quote: The lawsuit alleges that Flock also failed to put safeguards in place to prevent illegal surveillance by officers by accepting free-text-field entries instead of specific case numbers or investigations.
The only justifications entered for the searches of Mr. Murkerson's vehicle were 'info' and '37.' Neither corresponds to any investigation, case, incident, or call for service.
In August 2026, Flock announced it would change its software and require 'case codes for all law enforcement searches by the end of the year' as a way to mitigate these abuses.
three employees had resigned before the audit was completed
